description.zh: 1932 年 1 月 28 日夜，日军海军陆战队自虹口租界向闸北进攻，第十九路军奋起抵抗，一·二八淞沪抗战爆发。原线起点画在长江口外，与事变地点无关；现改为虹口至闸北的进攻段。
description.en: On the night of 28 January 1932 Japanese marines advanced from the Hongkou concession into Zhabei, and the 19th Route Army resisted, beginning the January 28 defence of Shanghai. The former line began outside the Yangtze estuary, unrelated to the incident; it is now the Hongkou–Zhabei attack.

name.zh: 灵丘—平型关（日军第 5 师团进攻）

description.zh: 1937 年 9 月 20 日日军第 5 师团占领灵丘（今灵丘县，114.24°E 39.44°N），随即沿灵丘—平型关大道南下；9 月 25 日八路军第 115 师在乔沟伏击其辎重部队。原线起点误置于灵丘以西约 60 公里，已改正为灵丘县城。
description.en: On 20 September 1937 the Japanese 5th Division took Lingqiu (114.24°E 39.44°N) and moved south along the Lingqiu–Pingxingguan road; on 25 September the 115th Division ambushed its supply column at Qiaogou. The former start lay about 60 km west of Lingqiu and has been corrected to the county town.

name.zh: 大同—忻口—太原（日军第 5 师团等）

description.zh: 1937 年 9 月 13 日日军占大同，随后沿同蒲路南下；10 月 13 日猛攻忻口，中国军队凭险坚守二十余日，11 月 2 日南撤，11 月 8 日太原失守。原线起点作大同但无前置，现补占大同并改为完整南下序列。
description.en: On 13 September 1937 the Japanese took Datong and moved south along the Tongpu railway; on 13 October they attacked Xinkou, where the Chinese army held for over twenty days before withdrawing on 2 November, Taiyuan falling on 8 November. The former line began at Datong without a precedent; the capture of Datong is now included.

description.zh: 1938 年 1 月 10 日日军在青岛登陆，随后沿胶济路西进；3 月起第 5 师团自潍县南下进攻临沂，与守军激战至 4 月。原线起点青岛无前置，现补登陆一段。
description.en: On 10 January 1938 the Japanese landed at Qingdao and moved west along the Jiaoji railway; from March the 5th Division advanced south from Weixian against Linyi, fighting until April. The former line began at Qingdao without a precedent; the landing is now included.

name.zh: 兰封会战（菏泽—兰封—开封）

description.zh: 1938 年 5 月 14 日日军第 14 师团占菏泽后南下，24 日陷兰封；中国军队 12 个师围攻未果，日军增援抵达，6 月 6 日占开封。原线作商丘—开封，与土肥原师团自菏泽南下的实际路线不符；现改为菏泽—兰封—开封。
description.en: After taking Heze on 14 May 1938 the Japanese 14th Division moved south and took Lanfeng on the 24th; twelve Chinese divisions failed to destroy it, Japanese reinforcements arrived and Kaifeng fell on 6 June. The former line ran Shangqiu–Kaifeng, which does not match Dohihara’s advance from Heze; it is now Heze–Lanfeng–Kaifeng.

description.en: On 27 August 1938 the Japanese 2nd Army moved west from Lu’an along the northern Dabie foothills against Shangcheng and Huangchuan, taking Shangcheng on 16 September. The former line ended at Lihuang (Jinzhai), which this column did not attack; it is now Lu’an–Shangcheng.

description.en: On 21 October 1938 the Japanese 21st Army, having landed at Daya Bay, reached Guangzhou via Zengcheng and entered the city that day, which then fell. The former line began some 10 km east of the city; it is now the entry from the outskirts.

description.en: On 2 October 1941 the Japanese 35th Division attacked Zhengzhou from the Kaifeng–Zhongmu area, taking it on the 4th; the Chinese counter-attacked and the Japanese withdrew in early November. The former line began at Zhongmu without a precedent; it now starts at Kaifeng, anchored by the departure event.

description.en: On 2 November 1943 the Japanese 11th Army moved south from the Gong’an–Shishuo area and entered Changde on 3 December; the Chinese counter-attacked and the Japanese withdrew in late December. The former line began west of Gong’an without a precedent; it now starts at Gong’an, anchored by the departure event.
